title: What are the optimal constants in the Ω(m^{2/3}) bound

problemStatement.plain: Formal investigation in graph theory: What are the optimal constants in the Ω(m^{2/3}) bound.

currentState.focus: Formalized optimal constant framework and proved structural theorems

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Eliminated both sorries. c4free_of_few_edges (edge counting via Sym2 distinctness) and optimal_constant_pos (BddAbove via Fin 2 specialization + le_csSup). File: 355 lines, 17 theorems, 2 axioms (deep results), 0 sorries.
builtItems: c4free_of_few_edges: graph with ≤3 edges has no C₄ (Erdos1008OQ01.lean:261-322)
insights: K_{2,2}=C₄ equivalence proved via Finset.card_eq_two destructuring
Common neighbor uniqueness is key structural constraint driving KST bounds
The optimal constant c* ∈ (0,1] -- upper bound from Folkman, lower from CFS
rpow_mul + norm_num sufficient for real power arithmetic (n³)^{2/3}=n²
SimpleGraph.ne_of_adj gives distinctness from adjacency (for irreflexive graphs)
c4free_of_few_edges proof uses Sym2.eq_iff to show 4 edges of a C₄ are distinct, giving card≥4 contradiction
optimal_constant_pos proved by specializing admissibility to completeGraph (Fin 2) to establish BddAbove, then le_csSup
